newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Fin Ministry says Sweden has no EMU opt-out.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Fin Ministry says Sweden has no EMU opt-out.

text.p: The Dutch Finance Ministry said on Wednesday it believes Sweden does not have the right under the terms of the EU's Maastricht Treaty to opt out of monetary union at the start of 1999, a spokesman told Reuters.

The spokesman stressed this was the view of the Dutch ministry alone and not that of Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm, who is currently chairman of the European Council of Finance Ministers and had made no comment on the matter.
"From the Finance Ministry's point of view, Sweden has no opt-out, they have just signed a treaty and there is only an opt-out for Denmark and the UK," the spokesman said.
He said this view was based purely on an interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty signed in 1992.
"Every democratic government can decide for themselves if they want to join in (EMU) or not but if you look at the treaty, there is no opt-out," he said.
"Minister Zalm has made no comment on this," he added.
Sweden announced on Tuesday said it would not join the European Union's single currency at its planned launch in 1999.
Despite this Sweden has sought to keep the door open for EMU membership at some time in the future.
Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said the project was too shaky and public opinion was solidly against membership.

He told reporters on Wednesday that the decision was the political equivalent of Danish and British EMU opt-out clauses. "Of course we have the right to remain outside. It is written on the first page of our convergence programme," he said.
Under Maastricht, all countries meeting economic criteria for economic and monetry union (EMU) are committed to join. The only exceptions are Denmark and the UK.
